welcome.description: Startup splash. If Plymouth is active during boot, Cinemate waits for it to hand off before showing this so the screen transition stays clean.

image.description: Path to a bitmap logo, e.g. /home/pi/welcome_image.bmp. Overrides message when set.

enabled.description: true broadcasts this hotspot on boot. false still serves the web UI on wlan0/eth0 if that interface already has an IP when Cinemate starts.

https.description: TLS for the web UI on port 5000. Off by default -- cinepi.local and the hotspot address can never hold a publicly-trusted certificate, so this always means a self-signed one and a browser interstitial. Needed for the RAW pane's folder download, which requires a secure browser context.

web_api.description: HTTP/UDP control API over the Wi-Fi hotspot (docs/web-api.md). A missing or partial block behaves as the defaults shown here.

allow_destructive.description: false blocks reboot/shutdown/erase/format over the API. The hotspot password ships as 11111111, so this defaults to false.

auto_preroll.description: Warm media automatically before the first take. See docs/storage-preroll.md.

recovery.description: Standalone recovery console (its own root systemd service) for diagnosing and repairing a Cinemate that will not start. Reachable over the hotspot at http://10.42.0.1:8080. See docs/recovery-console.md. A missing block behaves exactly as the defaults shown here.

token.description: Required on every mutating request once non-empty. Read-only pages (status, log, why) stay reachable without it.

allow_config_txt.description: false hides the config.txt editor. A bad config.txt can make the Pi unbootable, and nothing running on the Pi can recover that -- so this defaults to off.

config_confirm_timeout_s.description: Seconds to confirm a config.txt change before it auto-reverts and the Pi reboots.

sensors.description: Per-sensor hardware: geometry, HDMI output, name spoofing, phase lock, CineMate Log, and the sensor metadata database.

record_policy.description: Dual-sensor record policy. follow_preview: recording follows the HDMI preview -- a full-screen or pip-main sensor records alone, side-by-side records both. always_both: force both sensors every take regardless of preview. A camera token on `rec` (rec cam0/cam1/both) overrides either policy for one take. No effect with a single sensor.

database_file.description: Sensor metadata database -- every mode each sensor supports (see image_capture for the filter that picks which ones show in the UI).

settings.description: Frame-rate conform target, flicker-free input, and sync tolerances.

light_hz.description: Mains frequencies to derive flicker-free shutter angles from.

arrays.description: One block per cycle-able camera parameter. steps is the selectable table; free steps continuously instead, in units of free_increment. See module/parameters.py:REGISTRY for the canonical name list (iso, shutter_a, fps, wb, hdr_threshold_low, hdr_threshold_high, hdr_blend, hdr_gain_adder). shutter_a additionally has sync_increment, its own granularity used only while shutter-angle sync mode is on (`set shutter a sync`), independent of free_increment.

free_increment.description: Step size used when free is true, e.g. 0.1 for fine sub-degree shutter-angle control.

sync_increment.description: Step size used while shutter-angle sync is active.

image_capture.description: Recording-mode selection and legacy resolution/bit-depth filters. enabled_modes is the per-camera mode list used by the dynamic recording-mode table; k_steps/bit_depths remain as the backward-compatible fallback when no enabled_modes entry exists for a detected camera.

hdr.description: ClearHDR (imx585) whitelist plus startup values for the live knobs. sdr/imx585_clear_hdr both true exposes the plain and the HDR modes; set imx585_clear_hdr false to hide the HDR modes. imx585_clear_hdr_12bit/_16bit choose WHICH ClearHDR captures exist; image_capture.k_steps then chooses their frame sizes, exactly as it does for SDR. threshold_low/high (0-4095), blend (0-8), gain_adder (0-5) seed the ClearHDR knobs when a ClearHDR mode is selected -- adjust live afterwards with `set hdr threshold low/high`, `set hdr blend`, `set hdr gain adder`, or a pot/quad-rotary channel.

imx585_clear_hdr.description: Legacy single ClearHDR switch. Still honoured, and used as the default for the two per-depth switches below, so a settings.jsonc that turned ClearHDR off wholesale keeps both depths off.

imx585_clear_hdr_12bit.description: Offer the 12-bit ClearHDR captures, at every frame size image_capture.k_steps allows. Off by default: the 12-bit modes still exist in the driver and in CineMate's code, this only keeps them out of the selectable mode list. They are off because the sensor's HG/LG merge stops reaching the top of the container above analogue gain code ~60 (about ISO 800), so highlight range collapses at ordinary shooting ISOs, while 16-bit ClearHDR holds across the range. Setting this true restores them -- and renumbers the remaining modes, which the startup mode resolution handles by identity rather than index.

imx585_clear_hdr_16bit.description: Offer the 16-bit ClearHDR captures, at every frame size image_capture.k_steps allows. Delivered linear, with no compander in the path. Note that in the binned (HD) ClearHDR modes blown highlights render pink in the preview and the DNG thumbnail -- CineMate ships without the preview-side correction for the sensor's HG/LG merge clamp; the recorded DNG is unaffected. Drop 2 from image_capture.k_steps to be offered 4K only.

iso_max.description: Highest ISO offered while a ClearHDR mode is engaged; SDR modes are never capped. On by default at 1585, null lifts it. The imx585 driver caps analogue gain in ClearHDR at code 80, which CineMate's ISO steps reach at about ISO 1585 -- measured on the rig, ISO 1600, 2500 and 3200 all map to code 80 and record the same exposure. Above the cap only the preview brightens, because libcamera's AGC makes up the difference as ISP digital gain, so exposure judged from the monitor is wrong by that amount. The 1600 step is kept and lands on 1585, shown green in both GUIs to say the camera is holding it; 2500 and 3200 are dropped.

self_heal.description: Automatically probe the live preview after each launch and try to recover the flat-pedestal ClearHDR startup defect. Off by default: the root cause is unknown, every recovery action is unproven on hardware, and the detector cannot distinguish the defect from a genuinely flat or dark scene.

thumbnail.description: Embedded DNG thumbnail mode written by cinepi-raw's DNG encoder: off (no IFD1, no bytes, no CPU -- not playable in the Playback pane), mono (greyscale, lightest CPU), colour (RGB, moderate CPU), or jpeg (quality-85 colour JPEG, highest CPU, by far the fewest bytes -- scene-dependent). Accepts the words (case-insensitively; "color" also accepted) or the legacy ints 0-3. `set thumbnail <word>` changes this live, for the next take. Colour by default -- operator decision 2026-09-13 (final): paired with thumbnail_size defaulting to 2, colour at quarter size costs fewer bytes than mono did at half size, so there is no size/colour trade-off left to make. See docs/settings-json.md's "DNG thumbnails" section for the measured bytes-per-frame and CPU cost of each choice.

thumbnail_size.description: Right-shift applied to the lores plane before writing the embedded thumbnail: 0 = full lores size, 1 = half each side, 2 = quarter, and so on. Applies to every thumbnail mode, jpeg included. Changing this restarts the camera (unlike `thumbnail`), so it is a settings-editor field rather than a live CLI verb -- a Save applies it on the next start. At the colour default above: 0 = 1280x720 = 2,764,800 B/frame (+22.2% on a 4K 12-bit frame, +88.9% on HD 12-bit -- what CineMate 3.4 actually shipped with before this fix), 1 = 640x360 = 691,200 B/frame (the default, +5.6% / +22.2%), 2 = 320x180 = 172,800 B/frame (+1.4% / +5.6%). Mono is a third of each figure; jpeg is a stated range instead, not this formula. See development/dng-thumbnail-cost/FINDINGS.md and the 2026-09-13 hardware-log entry.

dynamic_resolution.description: Startup default for dynamic resolution: when the requested fps is higher than the selected sensor mode can sustain, drop to the best mode that can (see `dynamic_resolution_priority` for what "best" means). `set dynamic resolution 0/1` overrides this live and the override persists in Redis, which a later boot reads back in preference to this value.

dynamic_resolution_priority.description: Which axis of quality dynamic resolution gives up first once the selected mode's own class (bit depth + SDR/ClearHDR) runs out of modes that can sustain the frame rate. `mode` holds the class and drops resolution first (16-bit 4K -> 16-bit HD -> 4K SDR -> HD SDR); `resolution` holds the frame size and drops the class first (16-bit 4K -> 4K SDR -> HD SDR); `none` never leaves the class, so resolution is the only thing that ever changes and fps is capped at what the class can do. A substitute is never larger or richer than the selected mode under any policy. `set dynamic resolution priority mode|resolution|none` overrides this live and the override persists in Redis, which a later boot reads back in preference to this value.

enabled_modes.description: Per-camera list of the individual driver modes offered by the recording-mode table. When present for a camera, this replaces the legacy k_steps/bit_depths filters for that camera. Each entry identifies a mode by width/height/bit depth/HDR and, when the driver reported it, its sensor crop window.

aspect_ratios.description: WP-CM-6 (ASPECT-RATIOS.md), WP-CM-11. Per-camera aspect-ratio selection, keyed exactly as enabled_modes above: a camera with no entry of its own uses "default". Ships as {} -- an absent or empty entry means each camera defaults to the ratios its own mode table actually maps to, derived at startup (one ratio per mode, its nearest), so a fresh camera never loses a mode to a default nobody chose. A "default" list is still supported as a deliberate global choice and narrows like any other entry once set. Each value names ids from the canonical ratio table (resources/aspect_ratios.json). The mode table under this selection is the modes reachable by one of these ratios (within tolerance, or the closest mode when none are, unioned across ratios), further narrowed by min_mode_width, k_steps, bit_depths and the HDR switches. Ignored for a camera with an enabled_modes entry -- that per-mode choice is authoritative.

min_mode_width.description: WP-CM-6. Modes narrower than this are hidden (not removed -- they stay in the settings-editor's unfiltered mode table) from the dial and both GUIs by default. An enabled_modes entry for a camera bypasses this floor outright: an explicit choice beats a default.

custom_modes.description: Per-camera-name list of mode overrides/additions (F-298). An entry whose width/height/bit_depth/hdr matches an already-detected mode overrides that mode's fps_max in place; a non-matching entry adds a brand-new mode.

24bit.description: Settings for the 24-bit USB dsnoop path (RØDE NTG, mic_24bit alias)

16bit.description: Settings for the 16-bit plain-arecord fallback path (generic USB PnP mics)

hdmi_display.description: HDMI canvas, GUI overlays, and preview zoom/source/pip/anamorphic.

mirror_to_both_ports.description: Single-sensor only: mirror the one sensor's preview (with GUI) onto both HDMI connectors. The dual-sensor compositor already owns both-feed layouts, so this has no effect with two sensors attached.

default_hdmi_source.description: Dual-sensor HDMI preview source at startup. Switch live with `set preview`. No effect with a single sensor.

hardware_controls.description: Direct-GPIO physical inputs, channel-first: buttons, switches, rotary encoders, combined actions.

reverse.description: Swap which rotation direction increases the value.

wrap.description: At either end of the range, one more click wraps to the other end instead of stopping.

input_peripherals.description: Grove Base HAT analog pots and the Adafruit quad I2C rotary encoder board.

reverse.description: Swap which rotation direction increases the value.

wrap.description: At either end of the range, one more click wraps to the other end instead of stopping.

hardware_outputs.description: Direct-GPIO outputs Cinemate drives: the REC tally/relay pin(s) and the REC sync tone.

output_peripherals.description: The optional I2C OLED status screen.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so editors validate the file as it is typed.

action.description: A gesture action: the string "None"/"none" for no action, or a controller method call.

phase_lock.description: Enable the cinepi-raw frame-rate phase lock for this sensor (holds the recorded cadence on the nominal fps for stable A/V sync). Safe to leave enabled on multi-camera --sync genlock rigs: cinepi-raw runs the lock only on the master (--sync off/server) and the --sync client self-suppresses so libcamera's rpi.sync owns that sensor's VBLANK.

tuning_file_override.description: Override the libcamera tuning file for this sensor. Checked before launch: a path that is missing, unreadable, not JSON, or not a "pisp"-target tuning (a Pi 4 / vc4 file cannot load on a Pi 5) falls back to the auto-detected tuning and logs one ERROR line naming the path and the reason, rather than failing camera registration.

path.description: Path to a tuning JSON file. Relative paths resolve against the repo root (not the working directory); absolute paths are used as-is.

log_encode.description: CineMate Log recording target for this sensor. false = off (default, opt-in only). true = on, using the live source bit depth's default target (16-bit -> 12, 12-bit -> 10). 10 or 12 = on, forcing that target explicitly -- applied only when the sensor's live source bit depth actually supports it (e.g. 10 to force 16-bit ClearHDR down to 16to10 instead of its 12 default); never silently substituted to a different target. Only sensors with a sensors.json log_encode block (currently imx585, imx283) support this -- the setting is ignored on other sensors.

camera_name.description: Name reported to the stack for this sensor. Only consulted when override_camera_name is true.

override_camera_name.description: Report camera_name instead of the sensor's detected model.

geometry.description: Sensor read-out orientation, applied at capture.

output.description: Which HDMI connector this sensor's preview goes to.
